claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based BCC high-entropy alloy such as NbMoTaW.
The target solid exhibits complex local lattice distortion and possible short-range order.
Standard DFT thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive for this melting calculation.
Empirical EAM potentials fail to capture complex liquid structures in multicomponent systems.
Moment Tensor Potentials can be trained by active learning on DFT configurations for multicomponent refractory alloys.
The MTP training data should combine solid and high-temperature liquid configurations.
An MTP-based perturbation scheme can replace full phase-space thermodynamic integration for melting free-energy calculations.
The proposed approach is applicable at temperatures approaching and exceeding the melting point of a refractory multicomponent alloy.
An MTP can capture local atomic relaxation and complex liquid structure more accurately than EAM while remaining computationally efficient.
A fourfold speedup has been reported for comparable high-temperature free-energy predictions.
Errors below 1 meV/atom have been reported for comparable high-temperature free-energy predictions.
Active-learning-selected configurations allow the MTP to approximate the relevant potential-energy surface.
An accurate MTP makes the perturbation calculation converge rapidly and avoids extensive sampling of the full phase space.
Adequate active-learning coverage avoids patchy descriptor behavior and local-structure errors.
The workflow will predict Ta-based HEA melting free energies with less than 1 meV/atom error relative to DFT thermodynamic integration.
The workflow will require only a fraction of the computational cost of DFT thermodynamic integration and enable high-throughput screening.
The approach may fail when high-temperature liquid configurations or transient liquid ordering are absent from the training set.
The approach may fail for nonlinear electronic effects such as Fermi-surface transitions or for magnetic configurations absent from training.
Active learning is assumed to identify the critical configurations needed to represent the disordered liquid.

The hypothesis is falsified only if the free-energy error exceeds 1 meV/atom or the melting-temperature error exceeds 5 K and the calculated liquid structure factor also deviates significantly from the reference.
